Each version reports its measured width and what it offers assistive technology.

What splitting into letters costs depends on the text: an ordinary English sentence here gains about 1 to 2%, the line built from kerning pairs about 6%, the Arabic phrase about a third (its letters stop joining), and SplitType cuts the Devanagari word into parts. Splitting by words costs almost no width in any of these libraries, though GSAP’s link still loses its name. A plain inline span keeps the shaping only while the pieces share one style: change a piece’s weight or size and the browser shapes it separately, and the line changes width. Motion+ splitText is a paid product and isn’t run here; the paper reports what its published build did.
